data.description:
Krispy Kreme Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of Krispy Kreme, Inc. - DNUT

Former Attorney General of Louisiana, Charles C. Foti, Jr., Esq., a partner at the law firm of Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC (“KSF”), announces that KSF has commenced an investigation into Krispy Kreme, Inc. (“Krispy Kreme” or the “Company”) (NasdaqGS: DNUT).

On October 26, 2022, the Company commenced a small-scale test to offer doughnuts at McDonald's Corporation ("McDonald's") restaurants in Louisville, Kentucky, and the surrounding area. On March 26, 2024, the Company and McDonald's announced that they would expand the partnership nationwide beginning in the second half of 2024. On February 25, 2025, the Company reassured investors regarding the growth opportunities of the partnership and the potential profitability of the U.S. national rollout, and "remain[ed] on track to reach about 6,000 restaurants by year end."

However, on May 8, 2025, the Company disclosed that it was pausing the McDonald's rollout—the centerpiece of its U.S. growth strategy. The Company announced that it was "reassessing the deployment schedule together with McDonald's while it works to achieve a profitable business model for all parties and does not expect to launch in any additional restaurants in the second quarter of 2025." The Company further disclosed that, as of March 30, 2025, Krispy Kreme doughnuts remained available in just over 2,400 McDonald's restaurants, effectively unchanged from the total reached on February 25, 2025, revealing that the expansion had stalled almost immediately after it assured investors that it was on track.

Thereafter, the Company and certain of its executives were sued in a securities class action lawsuit, charging them with failing to disclose material information during the Class Period in violation of federal securities laws, which remains ongoing.

KSF’s investigation is focusing on whether Krispy Kreme’s officers and/or directors breached their fiduciary duties to its shareholders or otherwise violated state or federal laws.

data.title: 30-year mortgage rate jumps to 7.17% - a nearly 2-year high - in the latest blow to the housing market
data.description:
By Aarthi Swaminathan

The 10-year Treasury yield crossed a key 5% threshold on Monday, nudging the average 30-year mortgage rate upward

The 30-year rate is at the highest level since January 2025, when it averaged 7.26%. That month marked President Donald Trump's second inauguration.

Mortgage rates jumped to a 20-month high ahead of the Federal Reserve's expected interest-rate hike this week.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 5 basis points on Monday to 7.17%, according to Mortgage News Daily. The 30-year rate was up 23 basis points since last Tuesday, the first trading day of last week.

That puts the 30-year rate at the highest level since January 2025, when it averaged 7.26%. That month marked President Donald Trump's second inauguration.

Mortgage rates are up due to a combination of political developments, economic data and bond issuance. To be clear, mortgage rates don't directly follow the direction of the Fed's benchmark short-term interest rate; instead, they tend to move in tandem with the yield on the 10-year Treasury note BX:TMUBMUSD10Y.

The 10-year Treasury yield on Monday crossed the key 5% threshold, which in turn nudged the 30-year mortgage rate upward.

"U.S. Treasury yields often act as a benchmark for mortgage pricing, and we've seen yields move higher as federal borrowing needs expand and debt levels continue to rise," Ryan Hayes, head of retail sales at Chase Home Lending, told MarketWatch.

Financial markets are also sensitive to the conflict in the Middle East, rising oil prices (CL00) (BRN00) and inflation in the economy, Hayes noted, as well as "growing bond issuance from large AI hyperscalers [which] is adding upward pressure on yields by competing for investor demand."

Higher mortgage rates could cripple an already weak housing market. U.S. home sales are in a slump, and inventory has been piling up as buyers get spooked by higher borrowing costs.

"We're going to see the housing market slow significantly this fall. Rates near 7% will continue to freeze out first-time and moderate-income buyers, and more current homeowners will stay put to hold on to their lower mortgage rate," Lisa Sturtevant, chief economist at Bright MLS, told MarketWatch.

The housing market is currently in a "stalemate," she added, with buyers hitting their ceiling in terms of affordability and sellers not wanting to drop their asking prices further.

"Both sides are waiting for more favorable conditions," Sturtevant said.

-Aarthi Swaminathan

HelloNation Article Featuring Roofing Expert Cody Slagle Explains the Post-Storm Roof Checklist Texoma Homeowners Should Follow

HelloNation Article Featuring Roofing Expert Cody Slagle Explains the Post-Storm Roof Checklist Texoma Homeowners Should Follow

PR Newswire

DENISON, Texas, Sept. 14, 2026

The article outlines how homeowners can inspect shingles, gutters, flashing, and attic spaces after severe North Texas storms.

DENISON, Texas, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What should a homeowner do after a strong Texoma storm to ensure the roof remains sound? A HelloNation article provides clear guidance on how to address this concern, offering a step-by-step look at a reliable roof-storm inspection checklist that helps residents stay aware of early warning signs. The full explanation appears in a HelloNation article.

The article states that many people begin with the shingles because these pieces form the first line of defense. Roofing Expert Cody Slagle explains that shingles are among the first to show signs after heavy wind or hail. When shingles appear cracked or lifted, it can suggest that the storm pushed them out of place. Homeowners in Lake Texoma communities often face sudden weather changes, and the article notes that scattered hail can mark several slopes. This part of the post-storm roof checklist helps homeowners spot early problems before they grow.

The article also shows why gutter checks are important for a full roof storm inspection checklist. Gutters can show dents where hail fell with enough force to affect roofing materials. The article notes that sagging or loose gutters may mean water overflowed during the storm. When water moves back toward the roof instead of away from it, the structure can weaken. Cody Slagle understands how common this issue is in North Texas because strong winds often blow debris into gutter channels. This is why gutters appear several times throughout the recommended steps.

Flashing receives close attention in the article because it sits at joints around chimneys, vent stacks, and roof valleys. The article explains that flashing can bend upward when the wind slips under the edges. This small shift can allow water to travel into the home before the homeowner even notices. Roofing Expert Cody Slagle states that flashing problems can move water far from the entry point, making leaks seem unrelated to the actual source. Including flashing in the post-storm roof checklist is essential for homeowners across North Texas who want to find issues early.

The article also highlights the importance of checking attic moisture. A short attic visit can reveal interior warning signs after severe weather. The article describes how damp insulation feels cool and clumpy, while wet rafters may have a faint musty smell. These clues help residents near Lake Texoma understand whether wind or hail may have opened a pathway for moisture. Cody Slagle agrees that attic moisture is a vital part of any roof storm inspection checklist because small leaks often widen once North Texas heat follows a heavy storm.

The article recommends repeating the inspection within a day or two. Shingles that were damp during the first check may show cracks once dry. Changing light conditions can also reveal dents or small gaps. Texoma storms often come in quick waves, and the article states that homeowners should remain alert even after the first walk around the home. This repeated look helps confirm that shingles, flashing, gutters, and attic moisture remain stable. Cody Slagle often tells North Texas residents that follow-up checks help prevent minor issues from becoming future repairs.

The article also notes that homeowners can learn from observing their neighborhood. If nearby homes show tarps or roofing crews, it may mean the area took a harder hit. Storm paths often change direction quickly around Lake Texoma, so one street may face more damage than another. Roofing Expert Cody Slagle explains that such patterns remind homeowners to follow the full post-storm roof checklist even if their own home seems fine at first glance. Repeating the keyword phrase helps emphasize how important this process is across the community.

A careful review of shingles, gutters, flashing, and attic moisture helps residents understand their roof condition before problems become severe. These steps give North Texas homeowners a practical guide during storm season. When residents follow the recommended roof storm inspection checklist, they can better identify risks early and know when to call a professional. The article ties each step back to common weather patterns near Lake Texoma and shows how simple habits can protect a home.

The Post-Storm Roof Checklist Every Texoma Homeowner Needs features insights from Cody Slagle, Roofing Expert of Denison, TX, in HelloNation.

What is the Lincoln securities fraud lawsuit about?

The lawsuit alleges that Lincoln Educational Services Corporation and certain of its officers and directors made materially misleading statements and/or statements that lacked a reasonable basis during the Class Period from May 11, 2026 through August 9, 2026. Specifically, the complaint alleges that Defendants knew or recklessly disregarded that the Company's admissions process was not effectively converting enrolled students into actual student starts, and that the Company was allegedly experiencing a significant and undisclosed decline in that conversion rate. On August 10, 2026, before the market opened, Lincoln reported second-quarter 2026 earnings disclosing that student starts increased by only 1% year over year despite enrollment growing 9%, attributing the shortfall to fewer enrolled students than expected attending the first day of class and to observed changes in student decision-making that affected conversion from enrollment to start. Following this disclosure, Lincoln's stock price allegedly fell $10.22 per share, or approximately 24.93%, to close at $30.77 on unusually heavy trading volume, which the lawsuit alleges reflects losses caused by the prior misstatements.

Who may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit?

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired shares of Lincoln Educational Services Corporation (NASDAQ: LINC) on the open market between May 11, 2026 and August 9, 2026, inclusive, may potentially be eligible to participate in this lawsuit as class members. Because class membership and potential eligibility to recover do not depend on taking an active role in the litigation, affected investors may participate without filing any individual motion.

What is a lead plaintiff, and how can I seek appointment?

A lead plaintiff is a court-appointed class member who serves as the representative party on behalf of all class members in a securities class action, working closely with counsel to direct the litigation in the interests of the class as a whole. Under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, any class member who wishes to be considered for appointment as lead plaintiff must file a motion with the court no later than November 10, 2026. The court typically appoints as lead plaintiff the movant who demonstrates the largest financial interest in the relief sought and who otherwise satisfies the requirements of Rule 23 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. data.title: AI doomsday fears are arriving at the worst possible time for the stock market
data.description:
By Joseph Adinolfi

The months leading up to a midterm election are typically a difficult time for investors in the U.S.

AI fears are rattling the stock market.

The latest cracks in the artificial-intelligence trade are emerging at a particularly troubling time for investors.

Semiconductor stocks, industrials and other corners of the U.S. equity market closely associated with AI were taking a hit on Monday, after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned in a blog post about the need to slow the pace of AI progress for safety reasons. Several other AI luminaries, including Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have said they agree with Amodei's concerns.

Last week, Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon said in a post on X that he had left the company because he felt that the headlong race to develop AI with the ability to improve itself could potentially threaten humanity if the proper guardrails weren't put into place.

Also on Monday, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note BX:TMUBMUSD10Y touched its highest level since 2007, adding another entry to investors' growing list of concerns.

September is historically a bad month for stocks, and Septembers during midterm election years have a reputation for being particularly rough, said Hardika Singh, a strategist at Fundstrat.

"You have the 10-year [Treasury yield] at 5%, oil prices above $100 a barrel, and now these fears are cropping up," Singh told MarketWatch. "I think it's very worrisome that this is all happening right now."

Strong earnings revisions have helped to propel stocks higher this year - but with the next meaningful earnings reports months away, the lack of fresh good news could also create problems. Recent reports from companies like Oracle (ORCL) have been met with a lackluster response from the market, despite the numbers looking fairly strong.

"The lack of earnings right now is really hurting," Singh noted.

Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research, has closely studied these historical trends. According to his analysis, going back to 1945, the second and third quarters of midterm election years have registered the only back-to-back quarterly declines for the stock market, on average, during four-year presidential cycles.

Midterm years have averaged the worst calendar-year returns over four-year election cycles, and the steepest intrayear drawdowns. Selloffs so far in 2026 have been relatively mild at the index level, and the fact that investors endured a big momentum selloff in July could mean that losses later in the year will be more contained, Singh said. 

 
Presidential cycle        Average price % change                         Frequency  of advance                       Average % drawdown 
                          Q1                      Q2    Q3    Q4   Year  Q1                     Q2   Q3   Q4   Year 
Year 1                    0                       3.2   1.5   4.1  9.5   52%                    62%  67%  80%  65%   -12.9 
Year 2                    0.8                     -2.6  -0.8  6.4  3.8   45%                    50%  60%  85%  55%   -18 
Year 3                    7.0                     4.7   0.4   3.8  16.3  90%                    75%  55%  75%  85%   -11.4 
Year 4                    0.6                     3.2   1.2   2.3  6.8   58%                    68%  58%  79%  79%   -12.9 
All Years                 2.0                     2.0   0.5   4.2  9.1   62%                    63%  59%  80%  71%   -13.8 
Source: CFRA, S&P Global

To be sure, the sense of panic that had rattled major U.S. equity indexes early on Monday was already fading in afternoon trading. Semiconductor stocks like Nvidia (NVDA) and industrial names like Caterpillar (CAT) remained under significant pressure. But strong gains for shares of cybersecurity stocks like CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD), and hyperscalers Microsoft (MSFT) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG), were helping to pick up the slack.

That other stocks have frequently rallied when AI-linked names have struggled has helped to limit pain at the index level this year. The S&P 500 SPX finished only marginally lower in July, even as the U.S. equity market saw one of the biggest drawdowns for highflying momentum stocks in recent memory.

Popular risk indicators remained relatively contained, raising the risk that investors might be feeling complacent about all of these risks.

The Cboe Volatility Index VIX, known as the VIX or Wall Street's "fear gauge," remains relatively tame, and corporate credit spreads have seen only a modest pickup despite simmering concerns about aggressive debt issuance to finance the AI build-out.

The share of S&P 500 companies trading above their 20-day moving average - viewed as a short-term trend tracker - has tumbled over the past few weeks, a sign that rising bond yields might start to exert more widespread pressure on the market. And with the Federal Reserve widely expected to deliver an interest-rate hike later this week, it is worth keeping in mind that near-term returns for the S&P 500 following a hike have also been tepid, Singh said.

"Higher yields have unraveled some of the diversification that we saw this summer," she added.

Meanwhile, any pain investors experience over the coming months may well be-short lived. While the run-up to Election Day is often turbulent, the months that follow typically see much stronger performance.

"It adds to the uncertainty, which is what causes the volatility and the average decline in the market leading up to the election," Stovall told MarketWatch. "Once it has run its course, then that's when the market tends to advance."

-Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: Jamf Announces Same-Day Support For macOS Golden Gate 27, iOS 27 And Other OS 27 Releases
data.description:
Jamf Announces Same-Day Support For macOS Golden Gate 27, iOS 27 And Other OS 27 Releases

Marking 15 consecutive years of offering same-day support, Jamf continues helping organizations succeed with Apple

Jamf, the standard in managing and securing Apple at work, announced same-day support for Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27, iOS 27, iPadOS 27, tvOS 27, visionOS 27, and watchOS 27, which became generally available today. Jamf delivers consistent and reliable support to promote business continuity for organizations that opt to upgrade immediately. Through extensive testing in Apple’s beta releases, Jamf ensures compatibility for all of Apple’s fall releases across its security and management platform – and has done so for 15 consecutive years.

"Apple sets the pace of innovation, and it's our job to keep up without slowing our customers down," said Akash Kamath, Chief Technology Officer at Jamf. "Same-day support for OS 27 reflects years of engineering discipline behind the scenes. Our goal is simple: give IT and security teams the confidence to deploy immediately and give employees uninterrupted access to the tools they depend on."

The following OS 27 features are just some of the enterprise capabilities supported by Jamf on day one:

App and security controls

Jamf's same-day support gives admins tighter, more native control over app behavior and device security. Allow/Deny Binaries gives security teams native, process-level app control enforced by macOS itself, with no custom scripts or third-party tooling required. Privacy Management in Apps, alongside new Website Permissions in Safari, collapses multiple permission prompts into one, so admins configure access once and employees see a single, clean prompt instead of a stream of interruptions. And for organizations deploying Apple Vision Pro, new visionOS Restrictions give IT teams control over device behavior, including the ability to allow or restrict Bluetooth modification and iMessage usage.

Software and infrastructure lifecycle

Support also extends declarative management to how software and content get deployed and removed across the fleet. Package Uninstall closes the loop on software lifecycle by removing software when its configuration is removed, eliminating orphaned installs. Caching Service brings granular, declarative control over local content caching, easing network strain during large-scale updates and app deployments.

Real-time fleet visibility

Admins also get a clearer, faster picture of device health and status without waiting for a device to check in. The Extended Status Channel confirms that configuration landed on a device during enrollment, before it ever reaches an end user. Fleet Monitoring surfaces hardware health data (including camera, display and more) for iOS and iPadOS devices, helping IT catch failures before they take a worker off the floor. Enhanced Logging lets admins remotely trigger diagnostic collection for troubleshooting with no user involvement required, a meaningful gain for remote and shared-device environments. And a new Lockdown Mode Status field lets admins report on which devices have Apple's extreme protection mode active while the setting itself remains user-controlled.

Compatibility with Apple's latest operating systems matters for two main reasons: it closes the door on vulnerabilities in out-of-date software, and it lets organizations upgrade without disrupting existing management and security workflows. Jamf's entire security and management platform is compatible with macOS 27 Golden Gate, iOS 27, iPadOS 27, tvOS 27, visionOS 27 and watchOS 27 from day one.

About Jamf

Jamf's purpose is to simplify work by helping organizations manage and secure Apple devices while delivering an experience end users love and organizations trust. Built for the AI-enabled Apple enterprise, the Jamf platform provides a complete management and security solution with autonomous endpoint management and AI governance across cloud and on-device models. Today, Jamf helps over 78,000 organizations across 100 countries manage and secure over 35 million devices. To learn more, visit www.jamf.com.

data.title: AI companies say they want to slow down. Here's how Washington might help apply the brakes.
data.description:
By Victor Reklaitis

Washington is likely to move slowly, but there are catalysts that could make it act faster than expected

What's coming from Washington that might rein in the top AI companies?

The hot topic right now is how to tap the brakes on the development of artificial intelligence - including whether Washington will jump in to do it.

The bottom line is that the Trump White House and the Republican-controlled Congress don't look likely to act soon, but there are factors that could make them move faster than expected.

President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson aren't pushing for quick action, so investors shouldn't get caught up in thinking that new regulation is imminent, according to analysts at Wolfe Research.

Investors "should take headlines suggesting a possibility of near-term legislative action with a big handful of salt," because "none of the bills floating around Congress are close to having the support necessary to get enacted," Wolfe analysts Tobin Marcus and Chutong Zhu wrote in a note.

While "some legislators' minds have been newly focused by recent developments, with dozens of members of Congress calling for some kind of action on AI regulation," reaching an agreement "that something should be done is a far cry from agreement on what should be done," wrote Marcus and Zhu.

The Trump White House is likely to convene a meeting of the top AI developers, and that may help Claude parent Anthropic, ChatGPT parent OpenAI and Gemini parent Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) with their "own efforts to coordinate on 'pacing the frontier,'" the analysts added, but Trump and his aides won't try to slow down the frontier labs "beyond what the labs are proposing to do themselves." The three top developers all expressed support over the weekend for slowing the pace of development due to concerns about catastrophic risks, such as the misuse of AI for cyberattacks or bioterrorism.

Both Democrats and Republicans will be "running on much more overtly AI-skeptical platforms in 2028," but there won't be concrete policy change until a new president is inaugurated in January 2029, Wolfe's team reckons. While Democrats hope to take control of the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate in this November's midterm elections, Trump would be able to veto any legislation that can't get the support of a two-thirds majority in each chamber of Congress.

Disaster or businesses could move D.C.

The earliest that new legislation targeting AI could get traction is December, when the midterms are over, according to 22V Research analyst Kim Wallace. But he said that it's more likely that congressional action will come in the first half of next year, although one thing that could move up that timeline is a "systemic catastrophe." Beyond the misuse of AI for cyberattacks or bioterrorism, developers have said they're worried about losing control of AI systems as well as serious economic disruptions due to AI.

The "business community, particularly banks and Big Tech companies" may be able to apply pressure on Trump and his aides and get them to take a more hands-on approach, said Evercore ISI analysts led by Sarah Bianchi, in a note.

"The administration did move on this issue last June - establishing a voluntary, up-to-30-day national security pre-release review of the most advanced models - after banks and tech companies raised concerns," Bianchi and her colleagues noted.

Trump doubled down on his largely hands-off approach in social-media posts on Monday after expressing doubts about the need for any guardrails on AI while speaking to reporters on Sunday. The president said in one post that the "only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades," adding that he and his aides "already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies."

Trump also said the thinks there is "a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China." Trump and others who oppose new limits on AI often have argued that China's authoritarian regime isn't imposing any restrictions, so additional American regulations could help Beijing's AI developers leap ahead of the top American companies.

The Trump administration "professes to be anti-regulation," but there are nuances to the current situation for AI, said Capital Alpha Partners analyst Robert Kaminski in a note.

"The effective White House ban of Mythos 5 & Fable 5 this summer demonstrated that export-control laws already provide an effective policy 'kill switch,'" Kaminski wrote. The administration, in fact, "seeks to mitigate potential national-security and cybersecurity problems."

Johnson, the House speaker, said on Sunday that Congress shouldn't impose an emergency moratorium on AI development even as he said lawmakers should show a sense of urgency.

"We have got to do this in a very thoughtful, deliberate way, and we have to do it with urgency. And I'm committed to that, as everybody else is," the Louisiana Republican said in a CNN interview.

Johnson told reporters on Monday that he expects a meeting with AI executives at the end of this week or early next week.

What bills are proposed so far?

The legislation targeting AI includes a measure that's being developed by Republican Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas, Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota and Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a South Dakota Republican. Cruz said last week in a social-media post that their bill aims to "address catastrophic risks involving biological or nuclear threats." In addition, Cruz expressed a need for guardrails while stressing the importance of beating China in the AI race.

"We cannot stick our heads in the sand and pretend this technology isn't happening. We need guardrails. But America needs to lead. If China leads the world in AI, the whole world is in trouble," Cruz wrote.

Meanwhile, Sen. Bernie Sanders, a Vermont independent who typically votes with Democrats, has backed a bill that would temporarily pause the development of advanced AI and permanently ban the development and deployment of "superintelligent" AI.

Another bill from Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and Republican Sen. Josh Hawley of Missouri promises to ensure there is testing and oversight of the most advanced AI systems.

The main U.S. stock indexes SPX DJIA COMP were losing ground on Monday, with the drop blamed on the AI industry's calls for a slowdown, as well as on rising oil prices.

The booming AI industry has been a major driver of the U.S. stock market's recent gains. It also has been helping to expand the U.S. economy, and so far there isn't evidence that it's causing the widespread unemployment that many economists have been fearing.

-Victor Reklaitis

data.title: PROPERTY MELD EXPANDS PROPERTY MAINTENANCE OPERATIONS WITH RENTCHECK INTEGRATION
data.description:
PROPERTY MELD EXPANDS PROPERTY MAINTENANCE OPERATIONS WITH RENTCHECK INTEGRATION

PROPERTY MELD EXPANDS PROPERTY MAINTENANCE OPERATIONS WITH RENTCHECK INTEGRATION

PR Newswire

RAPID CITY, S.D., Sept. 14, 2026

RAPID CITY, S.D., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Property Meld is expanding its property maintenance operations ecosystem, Nexus, with the addition of RentCheck, giving property managers another way to connect property inspections and condition insights directly to their maintenance operations.

This partnership represents a larger commitment in expanding property maintenance operations by connecting the data, technology, vendors, and services that influence how maintenance decisions are made. Every interaction with a property creates information that can help operators understand what is happening within their homes and portfolios. Nexus connects that information into property maintenance operations, where it can drive smarter decisions and better outcomes.

"Data has the ability to completely change how property managers approach maintenance, but only if that data is connected to the decisions being made every day," said Ray Hespen, CEO and Co-Founder of Property Meld. "Inspection data gives operators another layer of visibility into the condition of their properties. Bringing that into the maintenance operation through partners like RentCheck helps teams make more informed decisions, improve maintenance outcomes, and ultimately better protect the performance of the assets they manage."

The integration reflects Property Meld's continued investment in Nexus, its growing ecosystem of technology partners, vendors, and services supporting property maintenance operations. Nexus expands the solutions available to property managers while connecting more of the information and resources that influence maintenance outcomes.

"We've had customers asking for this for a long time, and for good reason. Property Meld's own data shows that the effectiveness of work orders improves based on the depth of context available. By integrating inspection and property condition data from RentCheck directly, customers are going to see huge time savings and much better maintenance results," said Marco Nelson, CEO of RentCheck.

The value of the Property Meld and RentCheck integration extends beyond moving inspection findings from one system to another. Bringing property condition data into the maintenance workflow gives operators more context to make informed decisions, improve how work is handled, and better understand the impact maintenance has on property performance.

About Property Meld

Property Meld is a property maintenance operations platform designed to improve maintenance efficiency, visibility, and performance. Through connected workflows, communication, and performance data, Property Meld helps property managers deliver better maintenance experiences while protecting asset performance.

About RentCheck

RentCheck is a property inspection platform that helps property managers conduct and standardize inspections across the rental lifecycle. Through resident-led and team-led inspections, RentCheck helps operators capture property condition, document issues, and maintain visibility across their portfolios.

Contact: Liz Greenway, Property Meld
Phone: (605) 431-0265
Email: liz@propertymeld.com

data.title: Endpoint Clinical Acquires Bluefin, a Provider of Clinical Supply Forecasting and Planning Technology
data.description:
Endpoint Clinical Acquires Bluefin, a Provider of Clinical Supply Forecasting and Planning Technology

Endpoint Clinical Acquires Bluefin, a Provider of Clinical Supply Forecasting and Planning Technology

PR Newswire

RALEIGH, N.C. and BOSTON, Sept. 14, 2026

This acquisition expands Endpoint into clinical supply planning while keeping Bluefin independent and RTSM-agnostic.

RALEIGH, N.C. and BOSTON, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Endpoint Clinical L.P., a global leader in randomization and trial supply management ("RTSM") solutions and a portfolio company of Arsenal Capital Partners, today announced it has acquired Bluefin, a Boston-based provider of clinical supply forecasting and planning technology.

The acquisition expands Endpoint into clinical supply chain planning while keeping Bluefin focused on its core forecasting and planning mission. Bluefin will operate independently and continue to connect with RTSM systems across the industry. Endpoint will support Bluefin with global project management, implementation, quality, and customer support capabilities to help sponsors deploy the platform reliably and efficiently.

"Clinical supply planning is becoming more complex, more connected to trial execution, and more dependent on timely intelligence," said Nagaraja "Sri" Srivatsan, Chief Executive Officer of Endpoint Clinical. "Bluefin gives Endpoint a strong foundation in clinical supply planning while preserving customer choice across RTSM providers. Together, we have the opportunity to bring intelligence into every aspect of clinical supply, connecting planning, forecasting, enrollment signals, inventory movement, and RTSM execution data so every sponsor can make faster, better-informed decisions across all their studies. Endpoint can also bring the implementation discipline and support needed to deploy these capabilities reliably at scale."

Clinical supply teams have long recognized that better outcomes come from connecting supply plans to the data that trials generate in real time; the challenge has been bringing those data sources together in a way that supports timely, actionable decision-making. Endpoint and Bluefin are helping close that gap, linking supply plans to trial execution data so teams can anticipate enrollment shifts and automate forecasting rather than react to them. Bluefin will maintain its open, RTSM- and forecasting-agnostic model, which both companies see as core to advancing the industry.

"We're thrilled to be joining the Endpoint team," said Andy Maltun, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Bluefin. "The connection between RTSM and clinical supply forecasting is so natural that it's one of the first opportunities we discuss with every sponsor. Together, we are building a clinical supply intelligence platform that uses modern technology to automate manual work, reduce risk, and lower cost through optimized supply plans."

"This acquisition is consistent with our strategy of building technology-rich companies that solve meaningful enterprise problems for healthcare customers," said Mark A. Goldberg, MD, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Endpoint Clinical and Operating Partner at Arsenal Capital Partners. "Endpoint gains a path into clinical supply planning, Bluefin gains resources to scale, and the market continues to benefit from an independent planning platform that works across any RTSM environment." Arsenal acquired Endpoint Clinical in 2024 and continues to support the company's growth and evolution of its RTSM platforms and AI capabilities.

By bringing clinical supply planning closer to real-time trial execution, Endpoint and Bluefin aim to give sponsors greater intelligence and confidence in managing increasingly complex global studies.

For more information, visit Endpoint Clinical and Bluefin.

About Endpoint Clinical

Endpoint Clinical is a trusted clinical trial technology and service partner that delivers reliable RTSM solutions. Endpoint blends seamlessly into clinical trial processes by providing anticipatory and adaptive solutions to proactively mitigate risks. With decades of experience, Endpoint offers a deep understanding of the challenges that sponsors and CROs face. Its tech-forward dedication to innovation and high-touch services enable Endpoint to control the controllables and proactively generate speedy, strategic solutions, so sponsors and CROs can focus on running seamless clinical trials.

About Bluefin

Bluefin is a clinical supply forecasting and planning technology company focused on helping sponsors and CROs make smarter, data-driven supply decisions. Its platform enables organizations to forecast demand, evaluate supply scenarios, optimize distribution strategies, and proactively manage supply risk across the clinical trial lifecycle. Through advanced modeling and planning capabilities, Bluefin helps clinical supply teams improve visibility, increase operational confidence, and support more efficient trial execution.

About Arsenal Capital Partners

Arsenal Capital Partners is a leading private equity investment firm that specializes in building market-leading industrial growth and healthcare companies. Since its inception in 2000, Arsenal has raised institutional equity investment funds totaling more than $10 billion, completed more than 300 platform and add-on acquisitions, and achieved more than 35 realizations. The firm partners with management teams to build strategically important companies with leading market positions, high growth, and high value-add. For more information, visit www.arsenalcapital.com.
